Question:
Points \(F,\) \(G,\) and \(H\) are collinear with \(G\) between \(F\) and \(H.\) The ellipse with foci at \(G\) and \(H\) is internally tangent to the ellipse with foci at \(F\) and \(G,\) as shown below.

[Figure 1](figures/2025_AMC_12A_Q14_question_fig1.svg)

The two ellipses have the same eccentricity \(e,\) and the ratio of their areas is \(2025.\) (Recall that the eccentricity of an ellipse is \(e = \dfrac{c}{a},\) where \(c\) is the distance from the center to a focus, and \(2a\) is the length of the major axis.) What is \(e?\)
